text.p: Here are highlights of stories in Romania's press at the weekend. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
Business:
ADEVARUL
- Daniel Daianu, chief economist of Romania's central bank, blames sustained inflation pressures on slow progress in economic restructuring.
- Financing energy imports threatens to siphon off dollars from the local foreign exchange market.
CURIERUL NATIONAL
- The newspaper reports on the steady decline of the leu on domestic exchange markets.
EVENIMENTUL ZILEI
- A Finance Ministry fraud unit is threatening illegal cigarette vendors failing to obtain excise stamps with a 10 million lei fine.
General:
ROMANIA LIBERA

- Emil Constantinescu, presidential candidate of the opposition Democratic Convention (CDR) bloc, will launch a libel action against Corneliu Vadim Tudor leader of the nationalist Greater Romania Party (PRM). Vadim Tudor had said that Constaninescu was investigated by the Communist-era Securitate secret police.
- The Health Ministry cannot offer free flu vaccinations.
- The number of crimes committed by Romanian nationals in Germany fell in the first half of this year.
EVENIMENTUL ZILEI
- The newpaper presents new issues from "White Charter of Securitate" outlining the activities of the secret police against Romanian intellectuals.

- Judge Costica Ionescu, chairman of the Central Electoral Bureau, said in a interview that a single forged signature in official registrations would be sufficient to launch criminal proceedings and disqualify a candidate from the November 3 presidential election.
- Emil Constantinescu has asked President Ion Iliescu to convene urgently the Supreme Defence Council to consider the crisis in Russia caused by the dismissal of Security chief Alexander Lebed.
ADEVARUL

- A scandal has broken out over election observers. An investigation by the newspaper's reporters reveals that three non-governamental organisations due to oversee the electoral process exist on paper only.
- France cannot accept that Romania might be excluded from the first wave of NATO expansion, French ambassador Bernard Boyer says in an interview.
- The newspaper reports on a French citizen accused of sexually abusing two underage boys.
CURIERUL NATIONAL
- The military exercise "Cooperative Key '96", part of the Partnership for Peace programme, cost one billion lei, but was a success. ($1 = 3,302 lei) --Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 312-0264
